item.title: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials
item.description:
A Biden-appointed judge late Friday ruled that the Trump administration exceeded its authority by threatening to prosecute state and county officials who do not comply with its election integrity efforts. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson barred the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security from pressing local election officials to purge registered voters, withhold their ballots, or set their midterm ballots aside solely because they appear on a federal list of suspected noncitizen voters. The Trump administration has argued its efforts are motivated by stopping illegal voting by noncitizens. But Thompson found that the administration likely violated the Voting Rights Act of 1965, which prohibits “attempting to intimidate, threaten or coerce” anyone for assisting another person in voting. “One of the hallmarks of a fair election is the freedom to exercise the right to vote…
